full_judgment:
2. The background leading to the Rule, in short, is that the petitioner is a private limited company engaged in cold storage business. The petitioner for the purpose of his business on 08-06-1994 applied for loan from the respondent No.2 Agrani Bank Limited, Principal Branch, A project was accordingly sanctioned by the bank. The petitioner refused to accept the loan as the loan was given only for machinery purposes. Subsequently, the petitioner filed another loan application and the bank decided to increase the loan amount by order dated 27-03-2001 when the petitioner accepted the loan, an agreement was entered into on 8-5-2001 between the petitioner and the bank. On the basis of the said agreement the petitioner spent money for the project and the bank disbursed amount by installments. But suddenly the bank stopped financing on the project and subsequently in the year 2006 issued a legal notice upon the petitioner to return the entire loan amount within 30 days. The bank then published tender notice in two daily newspapers namely, 'the Daily Janakantha' and the 'the Daily Amar Desh' on 22-06-2006 for selling the mortgaged property which could not be sold on auction. At this stage, the bank filed Artha Rin Case No.32 of 2008 before the Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka. In that suit after filing of the written statement the Managing Director of the petitioner company filed an application under order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground that the aforesaid case is barred by limitation as per provision of section 46 (1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 (Annexure-G). The Artha Rin Adalat respondent No.1 by impugned order dated 10-06-2009 rejected the application relying on a decision of this Division holding that provision of section 46 of the Ain, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as Ain) so far it relates to the question of filing of the suit by the Bank or financial institution against the borrower within specified time is directory and not mandatory and therefore in any view of the matter the suit is not barred by limitation (Annexure-H). It is at this stage the petitioner moved this application and obtained the present Rule. 

 3. Mr. Moudud Ahmed, the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner after placing the petition, the impugned order and the relevant Annexures with it mainly submits that according to section 46(1) of the Ain the bank shall have to file a suit within one year if the creditor failed to pay less than 10% of the amount to be paid within one year and as such the suit is barred by limitation on that score since the cause of action arose on 30-08-2001 but the respondent No.2 filed the suit on 01-12-2008. In elaborating his argument the learned Senior Advocate further submits that in section 46( 1) of the Ain it has been clearly stated that notwithstanding anything contrary in the Limitation Act 1908 any financial institution shall file the suit within one year which means that there is no scope to condone the delay in filing the suit applying section 5 of the Act 1908 and, as such, the Adalat has committed an error of law allowing the proceeding to continue which should be declared to have been passed without lawful authority. It has been further argued that the Adalat also committed wrong in holding that section 28 of the Ain is not applicable in the instant case since it is related to Execution Case. Mainly on these grounds the learned Senior Advocate emphatically submits that in all fairness this Rule should be made absolute declaring the order impugned against to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 4. Mr. Kazi Rehan Nabi, the learned counsel by filing Vokalatnama for the respondent-bank, on the other hand, opposes the Rule and submits that the Adalat was absolutely justified in passing the impugned order in as, much as, the provision of section 46(1), if not complied with, renders a consequence which is not mandatory but merely directory. The learned counsel further argued that a question of limitation is a mixed of question of fact and law which can be decided at trial. Further he submits that this is not a fit case where interference under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure can be legally allowed. Only in the year 2008 the suit was filed by presentation of the plaint against which the petitioner did not even file a written statement but filed an application under order VII Rule II which cannot be tenable under law. On the forgoing point the learned counsel cited various decisions, reported in 38 DLR 172,41 DLR 490, 17 DLR 191 and 11 MLR (AD) 58 = 58 DLR (AD) 1. 

 carries a sense of mandatory implication as a consequence. In so many legislations, as we have found, the legislatures to make a particular enactment mandatory, used some phraseologies to give it a mandatory meaning. For example section 96 (3)(a)(b) of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 makes provision for depositing a legal amount prior to filing of a pre-emption case absolutely in a mandatory implication. The section starts with the words and phrases, "An application under sub-section (1) shall be dismissed". 

 12. Moreover, the case was filed in the year 2008 by the bank where the petitioner as defendant did not even file written statement. On such an initial stage bringing an application under order VII rule 11 of Code of Civil Procedure only on the point of violation of section 46 of the Ain on count of the section being mandatory is against rationale. In the decision of Ism at Zerin vs World Bank 11 MLR (AD) 58 = 58 DLR (AD) 1 it was held that a plaint cannot be rejected under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure either on the question of law or on fact before filing of the written statement by the defendant. 

 13. Further, in a recent unreported decision passed by this Division (Writ Petition No. 1108 of 2006) it has been observed that, a plaint cannot be rejected merely upon some superficial or evasive ground. The grounds must be specific and emanate only from the plaint and the plaint itself. In that decision it has been further held that noncompliance of section 46 of Ain renders a legal consequence which is not mandatory but merely directory. It was further held that even this issue of limitation can be further decided exhaustively at the time of trial together with other issues. On the conspectus, the submissions of Mr. Moudud Ahmed have no substance for the reasons as stated above. (All the underlinings are mine)
